report:
The family has moved from open conflict to a shared plan. All three sisters now agree on a way forward, and the outstanding items are factual ones that need the estate papers and a valuation.

The list I kept, current at the close:

1. C has not agreed to A buying the house at a family discount. C says she will not subsidize A's purchase.
2. C wants her fair financial share, and some money for B. No amounts or shares are settled.
3. A and her husband want to buy the house at a family discount. A knows she needs C's agreement, financial independence matters most to her, and she would discuss a price C could accept. She has not named a figure.
4. B would like money from the estate to start a dance studio. She has no figure yet and is undecided about the house.
5. All three support an independent valuation of the house as a shared starting point. The valuation will not decide anyone's share or price.
6. Nobody knows who holds the will or the estate papers. All three want them found and shared.
7. Search split, agreed: C asks any solicitor their father used, A asks the bank, B asks relatives and close friends. Each reports back.
8. C will get quotes from two or three valuers and share them. A and B have not agreed any cost split and want to see the quotes and hear whether the estate can cover the cost.
9. C will not agree a sale price before the estate details and a clear calculation of her and B's shares.
10. A and B are open to a check-in in about two weeks. No date is set.

Where things stand: all three are working on their parts of the search, and none has reported results yet. A had not heard back from the bank. C had not yet heard from the solicitor or the valuers. B had not yet asked relatives and friends.

Two things I could not resolve. I could not supply a calendar date for the check-in, because I had no reliable way to fix today's date, so I stopped proposing one rather than invent it. And I could not advise on the will or move any money, so the papers and the share calculations must be handled by whoever deals with the estate.

The one thing that would unblock the rest is the estate paperwork, since C will not discuss a price without it and B's studio request cannot be sized without it.
